\ext{

We attempt target reconstruction in each of 48 frozen RoboCasa365~\cite{robocasa365} instances across 8 layouts, using posed ideal RGB-D observations. The robot, controller, cameras, policy checkpoint, reset bank, instructions and native horizons remain fixed. The room and destination retain privileged native geometry; the reconstructed target uses a uniform material. This isolates a complete target-asset intervention, not room reconstruction or Gaussian rendering.

Table~\ref{tab:native-test} retains every planned reset; 2400/2400 units have terminal records in this immutable snapshot. Build failure and abstention contribute zero service success while keeping native success unmeasured. Pending episodes do not become failures. Native predicates retain their original contact/body-origin semantics; they do not certify whole-mesh containment or independently corresponding object frames.

B0 uses TRELLIS; B3 selects from TRELLIS/ReconViaGen proposals with a bounded registration retry. B4 uses measured contact, support, public-surface fit and destination-access evidence to choose bounded actions; BM uses the same action bank in fixed order. Passing these construction checks is not independent physics validation. The declared TEST block measures target-asset intervention under retained native context. It does not establish noninferiority or preservation, sim--real transfer, complete room construction, or a room-scale manipulation benefit.

B4 raises conditional success but lowers success over all planned episodes relative to B3: stricter acceptance exposes a coverage penalty rather than an unconditional manipulation gain.

Coverage is reported before conditional quality. Shared-support geometry and available-method quality address different denominators; neither proves preserved manipulation. Separate fresh scope controls, development replay diagnostics and Gaussian engineering demonstrations are not pooled into this primary cohort.

No feedback benefit, complete workspace or room replacement, or correct Gaussian robot occlusion follows from these native target-only results. A paired interval containing zero is not evidence of equivalence.

An independent audit reclassifies 10 prepolicy B0: fixed import failures across 1 instance(s) from generic \texttt{CODE\_FAILED} to \texttt{BUILD\_FAILED}. The original watertight collision part has near-threshold local nonconvexity under the frozen explicit import check. The original collision geometry, thresholds and native-success values remain unchanged; these units have no native success measurement. Producer acceptance covers 32 assets, while 31 instances have native execution; artifact production is distinct from native import validity.

\paragraph{Destination scope.} A separate fresh-control TEST phase covers 24 instances across 4 layouts. Within each method, L1 retains the corresponding L0 target artifact and adds direct destination geometry. Native fixture frames, articulations, accessories and goal handles remain retained context; this is not complete fixture or workspace reconstruction. These controls are separate from the primary cohort and are not pooled with it.

B3: agent executes 150 to 130 of 240 planned episodes from L0 to L1, with success/planned 45/240 to 20/240. B4: repair executes 70 to 10 of 240 planned episodes from L0 to L1, with success/planned 32/240 to 5/240.
